security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates LR.B/LR.H using an unsigned memory operation (MO_UB/MO_UW) in gen_lr() instead of the signed variants (MO_SB/MO_SW), causing the loaded byte/halfword to be zero-extended into the destination GPR rather than sign-extended as the spec mandates. This is a natural pitfall because the existing A-extension LR.W already uses MO_SL (signed), while the adjacent Zabha byte/halfword AMO instructions (amoswap.b/h etc.) use unsigned MO_UB/MO_UW — an implementer adding LR.B/LR.H support may incorrectly follow the Zabha unsigned pattern rather than the LR signed pattern.
security_spec.summary: LR.B/LR.H require sign-extended loads (MO_SB/MO_SW in gen_lr); using unsigned MemOp (MO_UB/MO_UW) per Zabha convention zero-extends the result into rd, violating the spec's explicit sign-extension requirement and corrupting CHERI capability values in guest registers
